title: Majestic Puzzle
summary: Improve the king before pushing the passed pawn, keeping Black’s own pawns from creating stalemate.

nodes.question: Why is b6 too early even though the pawn is passed?
nodes.explanation: Begin after the bishop sacrifice and exchanges: White has Kc8/a4/b5 against Ka8/a6/a5. Both black pawns are blocked, so White must preserve a legal king move for Black.

branches.title: Improve the king before the pawn exchange
commentary: Begin in the complete supported six-piece source diagram. The earlier nine-piece bishop plan remains context.
Kc7 frees b8 so Black can answer a later pawn check without being stalemated now.
axb5 uses the a6 pawn to remove the passed b-pawn.
axb5 recaptures with White’s a4 pawn and creates a new passed b-pawn.
a4 advances Black’s remaining pawn.
b6 starts White’s counter-race.
a3 advances again.
b7+ advances with check against Ka8 and threatens promotion supported by Kc7.
Ka7 is the selected king move while Black’s pawn remains on a3.
b8=Q+ promotes with check.
Ka6 is the illustrated escape from that queen check.
Qb6# is actual mate: Kc7 supports the queen while it seals the sixth rank and b-file.

branches.title: The king moves instead of exchanging pawns
commentary: Compare the source’s king-move alternative instead of ...axb5.
Kc7 preserves the winning pawn structure and avoids the immediate stalemate.
Ka7 is a legal king move made possible by White’s retreat from c8.
b6+ advances with check, using the pawn’s attack on a7.
Ka8 steps back to the corner.
b7+ checks a8 and prepares promotion.
Ka7 is forced in this selected route while the a6 pawn blocks the lower escape.
b8=Q# promotes with actual mate. Black’s own a6 pawn helps trap the king.

branches.title: Push the passed pawn before moving the king
commentary: Compare the source’s tempting pawn push while White’s king is still on c8.
b6 is actual stalemate: it covers a7, Kc8 covers b7/b8, and the a6/a5 pawns are blocked. Black’s king on a8 is not in check and has no legal move.
branches.explanation: b6 is actual stalemate: it covers a7, Kc8 covers b7/b8, and the a6/a5 pawns are blocked. Black’s king on a8 is not in check and has no legal move.

exercises.prompt: Why move the king instead of immediately pushing b6?
exercises.answer: With Kc8 and b6, Black has no legal move and is not checked. Kc7 frees b8, keeping play alive until the pawn can advance safely.
